desc:
Flutter app maintenance and upgrades keep your project building, running and ready for store updates. In one fixed sprint, Ecom Swift LLC upgrades Flutter, Dart and key plugins, fixes crashes and deprecations, and tests both platforms.

## Why does a Flutter app need maintenance?

A Flutter app needs maintenance because everything around it keeps moving. Flutter and Dart release new versions, plugins change their interfaces, Apple and Google raise their requirements, and phone operating systems update every year. An app that was fine eighteen months ago can fail to build today without a single line of your own code changing.

Ignoring this does not save money. It postpones the work and makes it larger. A project that skips several Flutter versions faces many changes at once, and the old plugins it relies on may no longer work with each other.

## What goes wrong in an old Flutter project

The first sign is usually a build failure after a laptop or toolchain update. Other signs are warnings about deprecated code, plugin conflicts that block the dependency resolver, and crashes reported on new phone models that nobody on the team owns.

Store rules add a second kind of pressure. Both stores expect apps to target recent platform levels, and a release can be refused or an existing listing restricted when an app falls behind. The details change over time, so the point is to check them against the current rules before each release, not to rely on memory.

## How maintenance improves your results

Maintenance protects what you already have. Users stay because the app opens, scrolls and does not crash. Reviews stay healthy because bugs are fixed before they pile up. Your team keeps shipping because the project builds on a normal machine.

It also reduces risk during emergencies. When a serious bug needs a hotfix, you want a project that builds in minutes on current tools, not one that needs a week of repair first. Regular upgrades make each step smaller, easier to test and easier to undo.

## What a good maintenance sprint includes

- A clean build of the project on a current Flutter and Dart release.
- A report on deprecated APIs, analyzer warnings and plugin status.
- Updates to the plugins that matter most, with notes on what changed.
- Replacement plans for plugins that are no longer maintained.
- Fixes for crashes found in your logs or crash reports.
- Small bug fixes and improvements from your own list.
- Testing on iOS and Android, including a pass over the main flows.
- Release builds for both stores in the packages that include them.
- A written report of what was changed, what was left alone and why.

## How we run the sprint

We start by cloning the project and trying to build it on the current stable tools, recording every error. That first run tells us how far behind the app is. We then agree a plan: which upgrades come first, which plugins are updated or replaced and which fixes from your list fit the package.

We upgrade in careful steps, running the app after each one, so a regression can be traced to its cause. The Basic package focuses on a health report and the most urgent fixes. The Standard package completes the Flutter upgrade, updates the chosen plugins, fixes a set of issues and produces tested builds. The Premium package adds performance and memory checks, platform target reviews, cleanup of unused code and a care plan for regular monthly work, which is quoted separately. Upgrading always carries some risk, so we test the main flows and tell you plainly what we could not verify.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Give us a list of known bugs and the devices where they appear.
- Share your crash reports or store console error data.
- Keep a copy of the last version that worked, tagged in version control.
- Plan the upgrade before a major marketing event, not during one.
- Decide who will upload the new build to the stores.

**Avoid:**
- Upgrading everything at once without testing between steps.
- Keeping an unmaintained plugin because it still seems to work.
- Ignoring analyzer warnings until they become errors.
- Starting a maintenance sprint with unfinished features on the main branch.
- Treating one sprint as permanent. Plan regular check-ins.

## Who this service is for

An owner whose app has not been updated in a long time and no longer builds. A company that took over an app from another developer and needs a safe base. A team that wants a quick, bounded sprint to clear the backlog before a new feature cycle.

## What we need from you

Access to the repository as a collaborator, your crash reports if you have them, and a list of problems you know about. If you want us to prepare store releases, we need a developer or team user in the relevant console. We never ask for passwords. We confirm the sprint plan in writing and tell you early if a deeper problem will not fit the package.
